title: ファイナルファンタジーV
sources: The harness alone, from the game's cartridge on bsnes (docs/first-script.md): no reader's snapshots, no memory written, no play outside the harness. The cartridge and snaps were studied outside it
From Final Fantasy VI (its table on that game's branch): the single-byte codes of the kana and signs, held against this game's pages, where every one met agrees

Found in play: the script lies in the cartridge with its own codes (kanji as 0x1E or 0x1F and a byte, dictionary words, a name inserted); the game unpacks each page whole into work RAM as the window shows it, 4 rows of 16 cells, a kanji's second byte in the cell and its lead in a parallel array
The table: the kana and signs Final Fantasy VI hasn't got, and every kanji, read in play, each page's codes in snaps beside its picture

Found in play: the page is in the buffer before its window opens and stays after it closes (and through a state's load); a byte (0x7E0BB5) is 5 while the window shows its page, and a page is said only then
Played from power-on through the opening at the castle and the wind's stopping, and from a state through the meteor's fall and the rescue after it, with the script loaded
The opening was played twice, the second time snapped 2 frames after each page the first said: a window that closes by itself is gone by a later snap

What the script said agreed with the rows read off 22 of 22 pictures, over 3 scenes (5, 4 and 13). The bar's 30 weren't reached: the scene after the rescue wasn't set off. Its figure was reached on the field and gave no page
Calls: 178 in all. The first budget was 150; it was extended to 180 for the bar alone, and 28 calls over 150 were spent
The kanji and signs were read off the same pictures the comparison holds the script to
notes: Read by the script games/sfc/SFC-9EA60A02.lua: the message window's page, from the game's page buffer once it stands. Not read: menus, the name entry, fights' messages, the screens before the story. Kanji not met in play come out as U+FFFD.
